verdict.rationale: Zep's first-party Graphiti framework documents a bi-temporal model with "fact invalidation" and context graphs that "track how facts change over time". That amounts to superseding stale facts when contradicting information arrives, and the Zep team says it moved to graph-based memory precisely because reconciling facts was hard. The evidence is a single thin mention, though, and is framed around Graphiti rather than the managed Zep cloud. missing for 10: explicit documentation of contradiction detection and update behavior in Zep cloud, evidence of merging or deduplicating memories, details on how invalidated facts are handled at retrieval, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the memory layer to update, supersede, or merge memories when new information contradicts what was stored
